free_text.inst.v2.D8: It gets the shape of the hurt about right and then it gets the good part backwards, so I don't know what to do with it. Home and my mother reading hard — yeah. Health reading hard — yeah, I know what I put in my arm. Big changes and hard passages, live right now — okay. And courage and my brother and sister good, and work and standing good, that's my whole life in two lines, I'll give it that. But then it says income and gains and friends read badly, and honey, I have more money than my daddy ever saw and a house in Larkspur and a Porsche with the whole universe painted on it, and I have never in my life been short of people. Alone, sure. Short of people, no. And the one thing it says is unusual for me is that living far from where I was born is bad for me. Port Arthur is what was bad for me. They voted me the ugliest man on campus and I got in a car and left and became Janis. Whoever wrote this had it exactly upside down. The rest of it, the temperament part, broad-minded and trusted and drawn to advising — that's somebody's uncle, that is not me. Also there were a lot of chapters it kept promising underneath and I never got them, so I can't tell you if those were any good.

notes: Answered as Janis Lyn Joplin (b. Port Arthur, Texas, 19 Jan 1943; d. Hollywood, 4 Oct 1970, accidental heroin overdose, aged 27), from the documented record: birth certificate time, Seth and Dorothy Joplin, eldest of three, Thomas Jefferson High 1960, UT Austin dropped 1963, San Francisco, Big Brother June 1966, Monterey, Cheap Thrills, Kozmic Blues, Woodstock, the Tampa obscenity arrest, Full Tilt Boogie, the reunion, the Landmark. Where the reading pulled and I refused it: (1) C1 — the reading singles out living far from birthplace as one of its few unusual claims and calls it bad; the documented life is the opposite, leaving Port Arthur is the entire career, so I answered 'gone well' at confidence 4 against the reading. (2) C9 and A19/A20 — the reading calls income, gains and friends hard; she was one of the highest-paid performers alive in 1970 and never lacked company, so income/gains 'gone well' at confidence 4. (3) A30 — the reading's temperament line (broad-minded, trusted, drawn to learning and advising) tempted a 'philosophical' tick; the record says outspoken, quick-tempered, bold, gregarious, so I left philosophical off. (4) A10 — the reading marks the father hard; the biographies make Seth the parent she was closest to, so 'close' stands against it. Where my answer happens to agree with the reading it was reached independently and I lowered confidence to say so: C3 inheritance (confidence 2 — she inherited nothing because she predeceased both parents, which is not the same as inheritance being a 'difficulty'), C7 ears/throat (confidence 2 — vocal strain is documented, but that same throat was her fortune), C5 mother and C6 home are documented conflict and rootlessness, not borrowed from the page. Genuinely under-documented and hedged: A4 hospital admissions (no clean record of a formal admission; answered 'one' rather than inflate it toward the reading's hard-health line), A8, A9, A29. D2/D4 reflect that the copy I was given contained only the plain-English page and the house lists — the chapters it kept referring to were not there.
